walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 1: Communicating Information and Ideas — a core area of GCSE English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 1: Communicating Information and Ideas brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 1: Communicating Information and Ideas.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which reading skill hunts specific facts?
options: Skimming
Scanning
Reflecting
Inferring
Register is the same as accent.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
A noun is always a person, place or thing.
By the word's grammatical function in a sentence — not its meaning. The same word can belong to different classes depending on use (e.g. 'run' as noun or verb).
Implicature is a kind of grammatical mistake.
Implicature is the same as the literal meaning of a sentence.
Meaning conveyed beyond what is literally said — generated when speakers obey or deliberately flout Grice's maxims. 'Some students passed' implicates 'not all', via the maxim of quantity.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
Register is the same as accent.
Register is just how loud you speak.
A variety of language used in a particular social setting — varying by formality, field (topic) and mode (spoken/written) to suit audience and purpose.
